title: Why it's nice to compete against a large, profitable company: their profit stream is a prison
summary: Jason Cohen argues that a big, profitable incumbent is a better target than it looks, because defending its revenue stream stops it from matching a cheaper, just-good-enough upstart. The exception is attacking a loss-leader, where the incumbent can outspend you and has nothing to lose.

principles.text: An incumbent's large, profitable revenue stream proves a big market, willingness to pay well above cost, and a slow decline you can exploit.
principles.quote: The profitable revenue stream is a prison. It's the Achilles heel that allows the little guy to win.

principles.text: Undercut a profitable incumbent on price with a new cost structure; a just-good-enough product at a fraction of the price can win.
principles.quote: A startup with new cost structures, new technology, and new ideas can be competitive at 1/2 or possibly even 1/10 the price, even if the product is merely just-good-enough.

principles.text: Big companies protect profit at all costs, so they won't cut prices to chase you, even if it means giving up on innovation or speed.
principles.quote: The goal of a large company is to protect the profit stream at all costs, even if that means giving up on innovation or speed.

principles.text: Price cuts hit incumbents' profits disproportionately, so they cannot follow a startup's deep discount.
principles.quote: If you lower top-line prices by 20%, your costs don't magically decrease 20%, so now your profits are 0%.

principles.text: Large companies are valued on future earnings, not growth for its own sake, so they will not sacrifice earnings for growth to fight you.
principles.quote: In the big-boy and big-girl world of real, at-scale companies, valuation is about total future earnings.

principles.text: Never attack an incumbent's loss-leader; with deep pockets and no profit motive in that line, they are the scariest competitor.
principles.quote: Attacking a profitable business on its loss-leaders is a terrible strategy, because it can use all its powers against you, plus orders of magnitude more dollars
